Page 1 — Newtonian Mechanics
Newton's First Law: An object remains at rest or continues in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by
a net external force.
Newton's Second Law: The net force on an object is equal to its mass multiplied by its acceleration. F = ma.
Newton's Third Law: For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force.
Momentum: Linear momentum is p = mv, where m is mass and v is velocity. The SI unit is kg·m/s.
Kinetic Energy: K = 1/2 mv². It is the energy associated with the motion of an object.
Potential Energy: Near Earth's surface, gravitational potential energy is U = mgh.
Work: For a constant force acting along the displacement, W = Fd. More generally, work depends on the component
of force along the displacement.
Power: Average power is P = W/t. It describes how quickly work is done.
Test questions: What are Newton's three laws? What is the formula for
momentum? What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s? What
is gravitational potential energy?

[Page 2]
Physics Test Document — Electricity, Waves &
Thermodynamics
Page 2 — Additional Physics Concepts
Ohm's Law: V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
Electrical Power: P = VI. Using Ohm's law, power can also be written as P = I²R or P = V²/R.
Wave Speed: v = fλ, where v is wave speed, f is frequency, and λ is wavelength.
Frequency and Period: f = 1/T, where T is the time for one complete cycle.
Density: ρ = m/V, where ρ is density, m is mass, and V is volume.
Pressure: Pressure is force per unit area: P = F/A.
Heat: The heat transferred to or from a substance can be calculated using Q = mc∆T, where c is specific heat
capacity.
Gravitational Force: Newton's law of universal gravitation gives F = GmImI/r².
